attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack essay, stated as his own assessment.

semantics.note: Faithful restatement of an unhedged present-tense observation about OpenAI's business model and GPT-4 running costs as of late 2023.

contract.note: Reading 'no clear business model' as no established route to sustainable profit fits the passage, which grants the revenue. 'Cost a lot to run' has no threshold. The plain reading is ordinary and fair, but the result depends on it.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous Fortune report that profitability and burn rate were unknown. The loss figure covers 2022, and the $700k/day figure is a rough estimate. It records uncertainty but doesn't show that obstacles to profit or material inference costs existed.
OpenAI's own announcement of customer price cuts. Prices aren't costs or margins, so this neither proves nor disproves expensive inference or a route to profit.
April 2023 secondary report of an analyst estimate based on GPT-3, not GPT-4. It doesn't measure GPT-4 inference costs in the target period.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows uncertainty about OpenAI's 2023 profitability and gives rough cost estimates for an older model. It has no comparable revenue and cost records, no measured GPT-4 inference costs, and no proof either way of a credible path to profit. The price cuts don't reveal costs. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met, so the evidence doesn't settle the claim.
